reasoning_thinking_help_lightbulb_toolti: What do Reasoning and Thinking mean?
reasoning_thinking_help_reasoning_desc: Injects an analysis prompt into the system prompt that instructs the model to respond in a structured, step-by-step manner. The model receives explicit instructions for methodical analysis.
reasoning_thinking_help_reasoning_effect: Effect: More structured, thorough responses through prompt engineering.
reasoning_thinking_help_thinking_desc: Controls the model's internal chain-of-thought: “Off” switches thinking off, “On” uses the model's default level. The model thinks in a hidden <think> block before it answers. The menu only offers what the model can do: a model without thinking stays off, one that always thinks has no “Off”.
reasoning_thinking_help_thinking_levels: Levels: some models offer graded thinking depth through their chat template; they appear as extra entries (e.g. “max” on DeepSeek-V4 = Think Max with a considerably longer thought process). They are detected from the model's chat template (embedded in a GGUF, the chat_template.jinja for vLLM). The choice holds per agent and model: when an agent gets another model, its choice for that model applies.
reasoning_thinking_help_thinking_effect: Effect: Deeper analysis through internal reasoning. Produces longer responses and more tokens — higher levels accordingly more.
reasoning_thinking_help_both_on: Both ON: Maximum analysis depth – prompt instructions + internal thinking
reasoning_thinking_help_reasoning_only: Reasoning only: Structured responses without internal thought process
reasoning_thinking_help_thinking_only: Thinking only: Internal CoT without additional analysis prompt
reasoning_thinking_help_both_off: Both OFF: Fast, direct responses without analysis overhead
reasoning_thinking_help_where: 💭 and 🧠 are there for every agent in the quick choices 🎛️ above the chat and on its card under “Agents”. A change applies from the next message on.

casus_help_tooltip: What do these actions do? — Casus help
casus_help_intro: The events collect what the watchers detect: motion, faces, persons, vehicles, animals and image analyses. Per event you can have a description made (✨) or all at once, bundled per occurrence, so that not every one of a hundred similar images has to be described.
casus_help_sparkles_body: Describes exactly this event: zoom and wide angle go to the first image describer of the describer list that can right now, with the recognised name as a hint. The description stands as a second line under the person. Purple = already described; clicking again overwrites. Only one analysis runs at a time.
casus_help_bulk_body: Describes every event without a description (motion, persons, faces), once per occurrence: events of a camera belong together as long as at most 10 s lie between them, an occurrence lasts at most 5 minutes. The describer sees a sequence of the occurrence's images, the description goes to all members. AIfred first checks whether the model fits on the cards; the chat model is never displaced for it.
casus_help_grouped_body: Shows one row per occurrence with a purple "+N" (that many further events belong to it); a click plays the occurrence's images. Handy after "Analyse all". Switched off, every event shows on its own again.
casus_film_tooltip: Watch the film — browse all frames of this happening as a series
multipose_subtitle: Capture several head poses in sequence — this boosts recognition when the person later does not face the camera straight on.
multipose_no_preview: Pick an image source — live preview will appear here.
multipose_pose_left: Turn your head about 30° to the left.
multipose_pose_right: Turn your head about 30° to the right.
multipose_pose_done: All poses captured — save or add more.
vision_settings_face_recognition_help: Detects + identifies faces from the watch-mode stream. Low GPU cost, runs independently of the VLM.
vision_settings_face_continuous_help: Default: only on motion — GPU-friendly, ideal for entrance / doorman cameras. On: runs permanently — useful when still subjects should be recognized (desk cam).
vision_settings_feed_visible_help: Shows an accordion with the latest background events directly in the AIfred chat — useful when sources are set to 'Background' and you don't want the preview popup open all the time.
vigilantia_badge_window_tooltip: Events in the last 10 minutes (rolling window — counts down when it goes quiet)
vigilantia_feed_disarmed_hint: Vigilantia is disarmed. Click the eye in the mode row to start background detection.
vigilantia_feed_no_sources_hint: Master armed but no cam configured for background. Open Vigilantia settings and enable at least one source.
vigilantia_plugin_disabled_tooltip: Vision plugin is disabled — enable it under Plugins in the menu
vigilantia_help_intro: Vigilantia is AIfred's camera watch: arm it in Vision → Settings, set per camera what it detects (sources), and look in live (Live tab). Events and persons have tabs of their own.
vigilantia_help_eye_open_body: Vigilantia is armed. For every camera set to background under sources a watcher runs while its active time window holds. What triggers it depends on the camera profile: plain cameras through the motion detector, edge-AI cameras through their own detection. In the chat the eye at the right of the agents' row arms Vigilantia and disarms it; the card beside it shows the newest event, a click on it the latest ones.
vigilantia_help_eye_closed_body: Vigilantia is off. No watcher runs in the background. A camera can still be analysed in the Live tab.
vigilantia_help_sources_body: Per camera: background on = it runs along when armed (within its active time window), off = it stays quiet. 🗺️ opens the zone editor; its trigger threshold sets how much of the image must change for motion to count.
vigilantia_help_motion_body: Image-based motion detector (OpenCV MOG2), only on cameras without AI of their own (profile webcam), at the background sampling rate. Writes a motion event when the change is above the trigger threshold. The zones of the zone editor (ignore, ROI) act here.
vigilantia_help_person_body: YOLO11n body detection. Runs on motion after the face recognition and detects whole persons, also without a visible face. Writes a person event; an alert goes out only when no face was recognised and the camera's alerts, alert type, quiet time and alert rules allow it. Who it is, the face recognition tells.
vigilantia_help_edgeai_body: Cameras with detection of their own (e.g. Reolink) report person, vehicle and animal themselves, by default through an ONVIF subscription. On an alert AIfred fetches wide angle and zoom at once; it does not react to vehicles. YOLO checks person alerts (an unconfirmed one goes on as unconfirmed), face recognition runs on the zoom. Motion detector and zones are off here, except blacking out.
vigilantia_help_face_body: Face recognition on = on motion InsightFace runs and writes a face event (known, unsure, unknown). "Continuous" = regularly instead of on motion, throttled (for quiet desk cameras). A change takes effect at the watcher's next start.
vigilantia_help_preview_body: The camera images live, per camera 🧠 vision analysis and 👤 face recognition to switch on and off. Independent of arming; the analysis ends when no page watches any more.
vigilantia_help_personarium_body: Identity management — all recognized people, add or remove embeddings.
vigilantia_help_casus_body: Chronicle of all events — filter, delete, bulk-cleanup.
vigilantia_help_multipose_body: Guided enrollment capture with different head poses — for robust recognition when the person doesn't face the camera straight on.
vigilantia_help_lifecycle_link: ➜ When does which model load? Model lifecycle
model_lifecycle_help_title: Model Lifecycle — when does what load
model_lifecycle_help_intro: AIfred loads several kinds of models, each by its own rule. The status line under the top bar shows what is loaded and on which machine. Before a large model loads, GPU-Orc clears the cards it needs.
model_lifecycle_help_base_size: Size: ~280 MB | Device: as the vision settings say (face_recognition: provider and card, "auto" picks one), otherwise CPU | once per process
model_lifecycle_help_base_body: Loads on first use and stays loaded until a restart; it is never unloaded.
model_lifecycle_help_base_triggers: Triggers: (1) Vigilantia armed and face recognition on: the watcher looks for faces on motion (or continuously), on edge-AI cameras on their person alert. (2) 📸 Multipose and assigning an event card in the Persons tab. (3) The re-match in the Persons tab. (4) 👤 face recognition in the Live tab. — Once loaded, the model stays, even when every trigger is off again.
model_lifecycle_help_person_body: Detects whole persons (bodies) on the CPU and takes no card. Runs only when motion or a camera alert starts it, and checks the person alerts of edge-AI cameras.
model_lifecycle_help_vlm_size: Backend: llama-swap with a describer profile (-visiond), on this or another machine (describer list in Vision → Settings); Ollama only as a side channel | space measured per profile
model_lifecycle_help_vlm_body: In the "On demand" mode the first request loads the model, in the "Permanent" mode it loads when switched on and at server start. ⏻ next to the model in Vision → Settings and the status line load and unload it by hand; otherwise llama-swap unloads it after its TTL.
model_lifecycle_help_vlm_triggers: Triggers: (1) An image in the chat that the answering model cannot see itself, an event analysis (✨) or a vision tool of the agents. (2) The "Permanent" mode and ⏻. (3) Burn-in of a describer in the describer list. (4) Stress prewarm during calibration. — Switching the model loads nothing; an old Ollama model is unloaded then.
model_lifecycle_help_tts_title: 4. TTS (TTS-Suite: XTTS, Qwen3, Piper, Cloud …) — speech output
model_lifecycle_help_tts_size: Size: 0.5-7 GB per local GPU engine | The TTS-Suite service starts the Docker containers (CPU and cloud engines need none)
model_lifecycle_help_tts_body: AIfred only sends text and its list of engines; the TTS-Suite picks a card with room, starts the container on the first reading and unloads it when idle. The calibrated profile <model>-tts-<engine> leaves room for it.
model_lifecycle_help_tts_triggers: Triggers: (1) The first reading after a cold start starts the container (Qwen3 about 18 s, XTTS about 33 s to the first sound). (2) Before a model cold-starts, GPU-Orc releases the engines on its cards. (3) Stress burn-in during calibration. — Piper runs on the CPU, no container.
model_lifecycle_help_stt_body: The STT-Suite service always keeps a model ready on the CPU (no card). The GPU model is loaded only by a recording that goes to the card, in a process of its own; after 30 minutes idle it ends itself.
model_lifecycle_help_stt_triggers: Trigger: a dictation when the STT-Suite's automatic list picks the card for it. While a large model loads, the STT-Suite takes the CPU.
model_lifecycle_help_llm_title: 6. Language models (agents and Automatik) — llama.cpp and vLLM via llama-swap
model_lifecycle_help_llm_size: Size: differs per model | Backend: llama-swap starts llama.cpp and vLLM instances; Ollama and cloud have their own ways (cloud loads nothing locally)
model_lifecycle_help_llm_body: llama-swap loads a model on the first request and unloads it after its TTL (~/.config/llama-swap/config.yaml). Before a cold start GPU-Orc clears the cards.
model_lifecycle_help_llm_triggers: Triggers: (1) Every message loads the model of the agent that answers. (2) The Automatik LLM loads only when it differs from AIfred's. (3) Switching the model takes effect on the next request.
model_lifecycle_help_vram_body: Several kinds can sit on the cards at once. Calibration (Settings → Start calibration) plans the space beforehand. When memory is taken unexpectedly, look at the status line first (language model, describer, STT, TTS and who holds cards), then whether Vigilantia is armed.
model_lifecycle_help_calibration_body: The full run boots every topology on the ladder (single card, card pairs, grid) with the largest context it can hold, measures short and long context and runs the speculation-depth k-sweep on every full-context rung. The winner is the shortest turn time at the everyday context (short and long point weighted, prefill via the workload ratio) — context ranks above speed; the fastest reduced-context rung is offered as the speed variant. Chunk and GMU counter-probes check the winner, then the operating point is persisted and applied to llama-swap. Workload ratio and everyday context live in data/vllm_runtime.yaml (workload_prompt_per_generated, workload_context_tokens).
model_lifecycle_help_calibration_resweep: Re-measuring measures only the topology of the stored operating point again, after changes to probe, drafter or kernel. The dry run measures and writes only the matrix. Both as checkboxes in the calibration panel of the settings; in a terminal: scripts/vllm_resweep.py.

audio_sources_help: Every folder under data/media/audio/ is a source (mostly a symlink to a folder of the sandbox), plus the streams of the plugin's settings. The index holds the tags the audio player searches.
audio_source_remove_confirm: Remove “{source}”? The folder it points to stays.

audio_settings_root_help: Only folders below it can become sources (no symlink leads outside either).
audio_settings_list_max: Cut lists in the spoken reply from
audio_settings_list_max_help: When a list in the reply has more entries, the spoken reply reads a hint instead; the chat keeps it whole.
vision_settings_sources_help: Toggle per camera — enabled sources run in the background once Vigilantia is armed.
vision_settings_sources_empty: No image sources detected — plug in a webcam and trigger a rescan in the preview popup.
zone_editor_hint: <kbd>Left mouse button</kbd> paints the selected type, <kbd>right</kbd> erases.   Red = ignore motion  ·  Black = blackout (GDPR)  ·  Green = watch only this area (ROI).
zone_editor_ai_cam_hint: ⚠️ This camera detects persons/vehicles/animals itself (edge AI) — when armed, no pixel motion detector runs here. 'Ignore' and ROI zones only apply where the motion detector runs (e.g. in the preview popup). 'Blackout' always applies.
zone_editor_live: Live — paint over the areas you want ignored.
zone_editor_offline: Camera image not available (source offline?). You can still paint on the black grid.
zone_editor_no_source: No source_id parameter in the URL.
zone_editor_help_intro: Paint areas the background surveillance should treat differently. Left mouse button paints the selected brush type, right erases. Use the sliders for brush size and grid resolution.
zone_editor_help_red: Motion here triggers no alarm (e.g. swaying trees). The image stays visible and is saved.
zone_editor_help_black: The pixels are blacked out — only black is saved and sent to the vision model (GDPR, e.g. public street or neighbour's property). Motion there is suppressed too.
zone_editor_help_green: As soon as green cells exist, motion is evaluated ONLY there — everything else is ignored (e.g. only the entrance path). Green takes precedence over red.
zone_editor_help_controls: Mask active is the master switch: off = the whole mask has no effect but stays saved (counter-check). Saving takes effect immediately in the running watcher.
zone_editor_help_blue: Live motion versus the learned background. Paint areas that flicker constantly (trees, reflections) with »ignore motion« — the measured percentage then drops. Set the trigger threshold so the normal noise stays just below it.
zone_editor_help_threshold: Share of the image area that must change at once before the detection chain (person/face/alert) starts at all. LOWER = more sensitive: small or distant motion triggers too, but noise (light changes, leaves) fires more often. HIGHER = more sluggish: only large/near motion triggers — a distant person may stay invisible. Calibrate with »measured«: read the value during the target motion (e.g. a person at the end of the path) and set the threshold BELOW it, but above the idle noise.
zone_editor_help_ego: When the CAMERA itself moves (PTZ pan, auto tracking), the whole image shifts — the system detects this global shift, raises NO alert and relearns the new view immediately (instead of showing everything blue for minutes). Its threshold (watch.motion_ego_shift_px in the plugin settings, default 3 px) is the minimum image shift between two frames: LOWER = even tiny shifts count as a pan — careful: a mast swaying in the wind then resets detection constantly (detector stuck in warmup = blind). HIGHER = only fast pans are detected; slow pans cause false alerts again. In doubt the alert always wins, never the pan assumption.
vision_settings_source_background_help: Watch in background — starts automatically at AIfred service boot.
alert_rules_help: Which detections go to which channels. Image text = VLM description. One alert per happening (cluster).
vision_rtsp_section_help: Add a network camera. Edit existing ones via the plug icon on their camera card above.
vision_rtsp_delete_confirm: Take the camera out? Its events stay; credentials no other camera uses leave the .env.
vision_rtsp_cred_hint: Credentials go into the .env, never into settings.json. Leave blank when editing = unchanged.
vision_settings_face_retention_help: How long face crops, motion frames and DB events are kept. Cleanup runs daily at 03:00 local. Default 14 days.
calibration_hybrid_tooltip: Allow hybrid mode (offload layers to CPU when the model doesn't fit on GPUs alone). Off by default — hybrid inference is significantly slower and calibration itself takes much longer. Enable only for models larger than the total GPU VRAM.
calibration_previously_failed: previous attempt failed — tick the box to retry
calibration_dot_done: Operating point for the main LLM present (this hardware)
calibration_vllm_burnin_title: Side-channel pairs (VLM + TTS on one card):
calibration_vllm_hint: Full run: measures every topology on the ladder, the speculation depth and chunk/GMU variants; 30–120 minutes depending on model size, occupies every card. Re-sweep: only the operating point's topology, about a third of the time.
calibration_vllm_resweep_tooltip: No topology ladder: the persisted operating point's rung boots with k=0 as the reference, the k-sweep runs with production sampling, the same turn-time rule decides. Useful after changes to the probe, the drafter or a kernel.
calibration_vllm_resweep_needs_point: Re-sweep needs a persisted operating point — run a full calibration first.
calibration_vllm_dry_run_tooltip: Measures and writes the measurement matrix (measurement-matrix.json in the log folder) but persists no operating point and leaves the llama-swap config untouched.
calibration_reset_vlm_cache_tooltip: Clear the VLM burn-in table. Next calibration re-measures each VLM's VRAM footprint.
stt_suite_hint: Engine, model and quality per device, the order of the automatic mode, the memory margin and the measurement are set on the STT-Suite's own page.
stt_unavailable: STT service unreachable — is the container (stt-suite) running?
stt_initial_prompt_hint: "auto" = built-in per-language style primer (enforces punctuation), empty = off, or your own text.

agent_editor_reasoning_tooltip: Enable reasoning — the AI thinks extensively before each tool call. More reliable for complex edge cases, but costs 30-120 s per turn extra.
agent_editor_cloud_model_hint: This system agent drives GPU calibration. It is not used in the chat — the calibration workflow invokes it when you select 🤖 AI as calibration mode in the Backend section. Based on VRAM measurements, the model iteratively decides on the optimal context and tensor-split configuration. Provider and model come from the same Cloud APIs as the main backend; the model list is fetched live. IMPORTANT: the model must support OpenAI tool-calling (the loop drives estimate/probe/finalize via tools) — plain chat or multimodal models (TTS/image/ASR) won't work. Stronger-reasoning models are more consistent but pricier. Only the English prompt is loaded, because tool use works more reliably in English with cloud LLMs; the German file only keeps the prompts bilingual.
agents_system_hint: They work in the background and cannot be addressed in the chat: Vision describes images, Calibration drives the AI calibration, the Automatik detects addressee, language and mode switches and ranks search hits.

Say e.g. “summarize {filename}”

or “translate {filename}”.
stt_bubble_saved_speakers:
📄 Transcript saved: {transcript_link} ({chars}k characters).

The transcript is split by speaker: [SPEAKER_00], [SPEAKER_01], … These labels are anonymous — diarization detects WHEN someone speaks, not WHO they are. Map them to the real names mentioned in the conversation (greeting, introduction, form of address) and refer to people by name instead of “SPEAKER_00”.

Say e.g. “summarize {filename}”

or “translate {filename}”.
